answer: An agent economy can require proof of elapsed time from a trusted enclave: before its first trade each epoch, an identity must present a signed attestation that it waited a real, unforgeable delay inside secure hardware, like a raven that cannot fake the dawn. The enclave's monotonic counter makes the wait sequential, so one machine cannot run a thousand waits in parallel. A cipher of honest time, sealed in onyx-hard silicon, costs every fake the same idle hours an honest agent pays once.
